subject: design

source.track: IGCSE · ages 14–16 · common content (1.1–1.8) for all candidates plus one specialist option — Materials (2.x) or Graphic Products (3.x); 50% school-based design-and-make project (Component 2)

note: Units follow the syllabus's numbered subject content: the common content (1.1–1.8) in order, then the Materials option (2.x) and the Graphic products option (3.x). Common-content principles anchor the foundational and intermediate lessons; option content and commercial manufacturing feed the advanced lessons. Component 2's design-and-make project runs alongside the whole program.

program.title: 1.1 Influences on designing
topics: User needs; where the product will be used
Sustainability (Rethink, Refuse, Reduce, Reuse, Repair, Recycle)
Existing designs; fashion and trends; society and different cultures
The impact of design on society and markets

program.title: 1.3 Communicating designs
topics: 1.3.1 Drawing techniques (freehand, orthographic, isometric, exploded, CAD)

program.title: 1.5 Material classification
topics: Ferrous and non-ferrous metals and alloys

program.title: 1.6 Structures
topics: Natural and manufactured shell, frame and mass structures
Forces: tension, compression, shear, bending, torsion

program.title: 1.7 Mechanisms
topics: First-, second- and third-class levers and linkages
Gears, pulleys and belts, sprockets and chain drives
Types of motion: rotary, linear, reciprocating, oscillating
Conversion of motion and changing direction or force

program.title: 1.8 Electronics
topics: Open and closed loop systems: input, process, output and feedback
Programmable integrated circuits; building and testing simple circuits

program.title: 2.2 Making processes and 2.3 Commercial manufacturing methods
topics: 2.2 Measuring and marking out; cutting, shaping and forming; joining; finishing; safe working practices
2.3 Commercial manufacturing methods and scale of production

program.title: 2.4 Product analysis and 2.5 Use of technology
topics: 2.5 Use of technology: communication, designing (including AI), making (CAM)

program.title: 3.1 Types of material and 3.2 Drawing techniques
topics: 3.1 Paper and card; polymers; foam materials; composites; smart, modern and alternative materials
3.2 Technical drawing methods; methods of communicating information; presentation
